findings.F1: The book is close to holding the coins, so it falls as deep as they do. It holds a long position on 98.3 % of bars, at a mean allocation of 1.07 when long. Its median trade lasts 75.5 days across 916 trades. Its daily returns correlate 0.93 with holding. Its deepest fall is -79.0 % against holding's -81.2 %, which with a yearly return of 26.1 % gives the failing Calmar of 0.33.
findings.F2: The panic signal is not rare. Its forecast rises by at least 2 points in 1144 of the roughly 1250 grid cells of 84 bars, about 91 %. On those cases the mean unusual move is -0.13 % (t -0.21), so the book's gain is mostly the coins' drift.
findings.F3: The two deepest falls are the long declines of holding the coins. From w12 to w16 the book fell -79.0 % over 485 days to the bottom, while holding fell -80.7 % over the same days. From w1 to w3 it fell -70.1 % while holding fell -66.9 %. The book stayed long through both.
findings.F4: Cases where the coin had already fallen over the prior 7 days lose. The lowest quintile of the 7-day return (mean -16.2 %) has a mean unusual 14-day move of -3.94 % (t -3.37, 201 cases), and its worst point averages -13.3 % with 25.9 % of cases falling below -20 %. The highest quintile (mean +20.9 %) earns +3.55 % (t 1.75, 201 cases).
findings.F5: Cases also lose where the week's volatility is low against its 60-day level. In the lowest quintile of the 7-day over 60-day volatility ratio (mean 0.55), the mean unusual move is -5.18 % (t -2.89, 87 cases). In the highest quintile (mean 1.63) it is +4.78 % (t 1.72, 87 cases), and it rises almost steadily from the lowest quintile to the highest.
findings.F6: Cases below their 30-day mean price lose. In the quintile furthest below that mean (-18.7 %), the mean unusual move is -2.23 % (t -1.73, 151 cases), against +2.81 % (t 1.66) in the quintile 6.5 % above it.
findings.F7: The forecast's own size barely grades the outcome. The top forecast quintile earns +1.50 % (t 0.77), the middle one -1.36 %, and two of the five quintiles sit at the cap of 20.

ideas.idea: When a coin falls over a 24-hour stretch and its high-low range over that stretch is a large multiple of its average 24-hour range over the past 30 days, it earns more than its usual return over the next 14 days, and the larger that range multiple, the higher the return, only while its volatility over the past 7 days is high against its volatility over the past 60 days, the excess growing with that ratio.
ideas.consequence: A trader would buy a panic only inside a turbulent week. They would stay out of sharp drops that hit a calm market, which sit inside the long declines that make the book's deepest falls.
ideas.name: panic inside volatility expansion

ideas.idea: When a coin falls over a 24-hour stretch and its high-low range over that stretch is a large multiple of its average 24-hour range over the past 30 days, it earns more than its usual return over the next 14 days, and the larger that range multiple, the higher the return, except when the coin's 7-day return before the panic is negative, where the deeper that 7-day fall, the lower its return over the next 14 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would refuse panic buys that come at the end of a week-long slide, which keep falling, and keep those that interrupt a rising week.
ideas.name: panic after rising week

ideas.idea: When a coin falls over a 24-hour stretch and its high-low range over that stretch is a large multiple of its average 24-hour range over the past 30 days, it earns more than its usual return over the next 14 days, and the larger that range multiple, the higher the return, the excess growing with how far that multiple stands above the multiples the coin showed over the past year.
ideas.consequence: A trader would treat only the rare, extreme panics as a buy, rather than the ordinary drops a short history makes look large, and so would be out of the market most of the time instead of holding the coin.
ideas.name: rare extreme panic rebound
